original_question: Let f ∈ End12 (Q) be a rational map of degree 2 defined over Q. (a) Let P ∈ P1 (Q) be periodic for f . Then P has period at most 7. (b) Let P ∈ P1 (Q) be preperiodic for f . Then #Of (P ) ≤ 9.  (c) The full set of rational preperiodic points satisfies # PrePer f, P1 (Q) ≤ 14.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.7: the specialization of the Dynamical Uniform Boundedness problem to degree-2 rational self-maps of P^1 over Q.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official statement and correctly identifies the ambient field Q, the degree-2 setting, the projective line P^1(Q), and the three precise numerical bounds 7, 9, and 14. It is essentially a near-verbatim draft of Conjecture 4.7.
missing_details: The paper states this as a conjecture/open problem, not as an established theorem; the refined version should therefore be phrased as a question or conjecture.
The notation should be written as End_2^1(Q), meaning the set of degree-2 endomorphisms of P^1 defined over Q.
It should be explicit that f is a rational self-map f:P^1->P^1 defined over Q, not just an abstract element with unexplained notation.
The point P should be specified as a Q-rational point of P^1(Q).
In part (a), 'period' should be clarified to mean exact period under iteration.
In part (b), the forward orbit O_f(P) should be defined explicitly as {f^n(P): n>=0}.
In part (c), the set PrePer(f,P^1(Q)) should be defined explicitly as the set of Q-rational points x such that f^n(x)=f^m(x) for some n>m>=0.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the terms 'periodic' and 'preperiodic' should be defined via iterates of f.
refined_question: Conjecture/open problem (paper-faithful form): Let f in End_2^1(Q), i.e. let f:P^1->P^1 be a degree-2 rational self-map defined over Q. Is it true that every Q-rational periodic point P in P^1(Q) has exact period at most 7, every Q-rational preperiodic point P has forward orbit O_f(P)={f^n(P): n>=0} of cardinality at most 9, and the full set of Q-rational preperiodic points PrePer(f,P^1(Q))={x in P^1(Q): f^n(x)=f^m(x) for some n>m>=0} satisfies #PrePer(f,P^1(Q))<=14?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4's discussion of uniform boundedness for rational preperiodic points. More specifically, it matches Conjecture 4.7 on p. 7 almost word-for-word, including the three bounds 7, 9, and 14. The nearby context first states the general Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture (Conjecture 4.2, p. 6), then specializes to quadratic polynomials (Conjecture 4.4 and Theorem 4.5, pp. 6-7), then to the odd family bx+c/x (Conjecture 4.6, p. 7), and finally to all degree-2 rational maps over Q in Conjecture 4.7. The notation needed to make the statement stand-alone comes from the paper's notation page, where PrePer(f,S), Per(f,S), and exact period are defined on p. 3. The sentence immediately following Conjecture 4.7 states that examples in the cited papers show the values 7, 9, and 14 are optimal.
